nodes.title: Character E-polynomials and weighted counts
nodes.statement: For a good action of a finite group G on a separated finite-type variety X and a one-dimensional character χ, define Eχ_G(X)=Σ_i,p,q (−1)^i dim Gr_F^p Gr_W^(p+q) H_c^i(X,C)^χ x^p y^q. Over Fq define the χ-count by alternating geometric-Frobenius traces on H_c^i(X,Qbarℓ)^χ. Its stack expression is Σ_[z] Tr(Fr_z,Lχ,z)/|Aut(z)| over [X/G](Fq). Fix the associated-local-system convention so that this formula selects the χ-eigenspace, rather than its inverse. Both realizations are additive for invariant closed/open decompositions; Eχ is generally only an additive map, not a ring homomorphism.
hypotheses: G is finite, every orbit lies in an affine open, and the action is over the base.
χ:G→C× is one-dimensional; identify its roots of unity with coefficients in Qbarℓ, with ℓ different from the residue characteristic.
Compact supports and the geometric mixed Hodge structure are essential for nonproper X.
proofSteps: Import constructible compactly supported cohomology and the geometric mixed Hodge realization through G-MHS. Apply the finite-group idempotent |G|⁻¹Σ_g χ(g)⁻¹g.
Use exact sequences for invariant closed/open pairs. Apply the stack trace formula from G-ETII to identify the alternating trace with the groupoid-weighted sum, including nontrivial rational torsors.
The tensor-product rule convolves characters; taking a single χ coefficient therefore preserves addition, but does not in general preserve multiplication.
acceptance: For G=1 this is the compact Hodge–Deligne polynomial and ordinary point count.
For nontrivial χ, the χ-count of a point with trivial action is zero.

sources.match: The cohomological definition and its quotient-stack expression supply the realization; the weighted expression corrects the missing stabilizer denominator.

nodes.title: Fractional Lefschetz powers and root systems
nodes.statement: Use the equivariant scissor ring K0^G(Var/R) supplied by LD.3, retaining its distinction from further equivariant representation quotients. Adjoin coherent positive roots of L=[A1 with trivial G-action]; any expression in use has a finite common denominator N. For a fixed prime power q, a compatible root system is s_r∈C× for r≥1 with s_1=q and s_(rr′)^r=s_r′. Extend χ-realizations additively and linearly over the trivial-action Lefschetz powers: #^(s,χ)([X]L^(a/N))=#χ(X)s_N^a and Eχ([X]L^(a/N))=Eχ(X)(xy)^(a/N). Root choices remain part of the finite-field evaluation.
hypotheses: R has the finite-type hypotheses of the realization in use.
Fractional bidegrees live in the finite-support rational-exponent algebra, available as AddMonoidAlgebra Z (Q×Q); only the necessary denominator subalgebra is used.
Use a fixed system s for general prime powers. No root-choice independence is assumed there.
proofSteps: Import the actual equivariant Grothendieck ring and its realization descent from LD.3/G-Groth. Form the directed union of finite root adjunctions, with the transition L^(1/N)=(L^(1/NN′))^N′.
Extend the already additive χ map by the displayed scalar formula, using that trivial-character L acts by a Tate shift. Do not turn the χ coefficient map into a ring homomorphism.

For q=p prime not dividing the order of χ values, Eisenstein over the cyclotomic coefficient field and compactness transport two systems by an automorphism fixing those values. Apply this only at the prime-residue points used in comparison.
acceptance: Re-evaluating at a different root system requires an explicit transport argument.
An integral power L^a has E=(xy)^a and count q^a, independently of s.

sources.locator: §2.5, Definition 2.16, p.525; corrections E1 and E6
sources.match: The root convention and formal Lefschetz powers give the comparison algebra; the published independence assertion needs the prime-field restriction.

uses.how: Encode rational sector ages while preserving the chosen finite-field root system.
Match L^a with the negative fractional Tate twist.

nodes.title: Equivariant Katz comparison
nodes.statement: Let R⊂C be of finite type over Z, G finite and χ one-dimensional. For separated good G-schemes X,Y of finite type over R, equality of the corrected χ-counts after every map R→Fq implies Eχ_G(X_C)=Eχ_G(Y_C). The same statement holds for virtual scissor classes.
hypotheses: Fix an identification of the character-value fields in C and Qbarℓ.
Counts include every finite extension of every allowed finite residue field. Shrinking and spreading are performed simultaneously on both sides.
proofSteps: Use the equivariant Bittner presentation requested from LD.3/G-Groth, not a nonequivariant compactification, to reduce virtual classes to smooth projective good G-varieties. Spread the finite list and all relations after shrinking R.

Use constancy of character Hodge numbers in smooth proper complex families to specialize to a number-field model in the relevant component; this adapter is requested from CP.3. Apply R01.5/frobenius-density and R01.1/brauer-nesbitt-traces to the resulting virtual lisse realizations.

Purity separates each integral cohomological degree for smooth proper summands; work in the Grothendieck group. The equivariant Hodge–Tate decomposition identifies the multiplicity at Tate degree −p with H^q(Ω^p), correcting E5.
Additivity returns the asserted equality for the original nonproper varieties. The required geometric MHS and equivariant blow-up interfaces remain explicit gates.
acceptance: For G=1 recover ordinary Katz comparison.
The proof concludes equality of Hodge polynomials, not an actual isomorphism of nonsemisimple arithmetic representations.

sources.match: The theorem compares character point counts and E-polynomials through equivariant blow-up reduction, purity, density and Hodge–Tate multiplicities.

additionalSources.match: The equivariant characteristic-zero blow-up presentation uses equivariant resolution and weak factorization, not an arbitrary chosen compactification.

nodes.title: Finite-denominator Tate roots
nodes.statement: For R⊂C of finite type and a finite denominator N, choose ℓ∤N. After shrinking Spec R[1/ℓ] and a finite étale cover R′ with a chosen complex embedding, the cyclotomic character has image in a log/exp neighborhood. The character exp((1/N)log χℓ) defines a lisse rank-one Qℓ(1/N) whose Nth tensor power is Qℓ(1); roots for divisors of N are compatible. With Qbarℓ coefficients one can choose compatible roots for all denominators, but only each fixed finite set is asserted to have a finite coefficient model.
hypotheses: The sheaves are on Spec R′[1/ℓ], not on all of Spec R.
For the Qℓ formula N is prime to ℓ, or a specific finite convergence bound must be supplied.
No fixed finite coefficient field is required to contain every ℓ-power root of the cyclotomic character.
proofSteps: Kill the finite torsion quotient of the cyclotomic image by finite étale base change and choose a sufficiently deep principal-unit subgroup.
For ℓ∤N, division by N preserves the log image and exp converges; tensor compatibility follows by multiplication of logarithms.

For the all-denominator Qbarℓ statement use compatible principal-unit roots of a generator of the procyclic cyclotomic image, with continuous Zℓ powers. This is an existence statement; the finite-denominator branch suffices for every fractional comparison.
acceptance: For N=1 obtain the cyclotomic Tate sheaf.
A proposed Qℓ-valued system of all ℓ-power roots fails on an open cyclotomic image: sufficiently high powers cannot hit a fixed shallow principal unit.

sources.match: The finite-denominator construction repairs both coefficient and convergence domains of the published argument.

nodes.title: Katz comparison with fractional twists
nodes.statement: For R,G,χ as above and finite fractional-Lefschetz expressions X,Y in the equivariant scissor realization, suppose #^(s,χ)(X_Fq)=#^(s,χ)(Y_Fq) for every R→Fq, using a specified compatible system at each map. Then Eχ(X_C)=Eχ(Y_C) in the rational-bidegree algebra.
hypotheses: A single finite denominator N works for both expressions. Choose ℓ∤N and finite coefficient models after the permitted common cover.
The comparison is in a Grothendieck group of representations; alternating signs remain attached to cohomological degrees.
At q=p prime, p is also prime to the order of the character values when transporting root systems.
proofSteps: Reduce to finite virtual sums of smooth projective G-varieties times L^a by equivariant Bittner. Apply finite-tate-roots and identify L^a with Qbarℓ(−a), giving geometric Frobenius eigenvalue q^a.

Use the prime-field transport from fractional-lefschetz at density-one prime-residue places of the number-field specialization. It fixes the character-value field. Arbitrary prime powers retain their specified root choices.
Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt compare virtual representation classes, including all weight pieces; do not discard alternating signs when rational shifts make weights overlap.

Apply the generalized fractional Hodge–Tate realization of Ito §5 to those classes. Its rational Cℓ(a)-period multiplicities and additivity are the requested G-HT adapter. It returns the shift h^(p−a,q−a), with the negative Tate twist, then yields equality of rational Hodge bidegrees.
acceptance: L^(1/2) shifts the E-bidegree by (1/2,1/2); its realization is Qbarℓ(−1/2).
Keep X exponents a_i and Y exponents b_j separate; no conclusion about actual ungraded Galois representations follows.

sources.locator: §2.5, Theorem 2.18, pp.526–527; corrections E1, E2 and E6
sources.match: The proof extends Katz comparison to rational age shifts with compatible roots and corrected negative Tate twists.

additionalSources.match: Fractional twists and the generalized Hodge–Tate realization on virtual representations explain the missing rational-period adapter.

nodes.title: Stringy E-polynomials and point counts
nodes.statement: For a smooth tame finite quotient stack X=[Y/Γ], use its inertia decomposition ⨿_[γ][Y^γ/C(γ)] and the imported age F(γ,Z). Set E_st(X)=Σ_[γ],Z E([Z/C(γ)])(xy)^F(γ,Z), where the sector E uses C(γ)-invariants in compact cohomology. Over Fq containing the required roots, set #_st(X)=Σ_[z]∈IX(Fq) q^F(z)/|Aut(z)|, with positive real q^F. Allow Γ nonabelian here; the integration layers specialize to abelian Γ.
hypotheses: Y is smooth separated finite type; the finite group order is invertible, with the chosen roots of unity giving the sector labels.
F uses tangent eigenvalues exp(2πic/r) with 0≤c<r. The alternative weight satisfies w(γ,Z)=dim X−F(γ⁻¹,Z).
The quotient-stack presentation, inertia and age constructions are imports from R09 and G-ETII.
proofSteps: Apply the imported inertia and age to the character realization at the trivial centralizer character; sum its finitely many connected sectors with the rational diagonal shift.
Use weighted quotient-stack masses over finite fields, including rational torsors.

Prove invariance under presentation and simultaneous root-generator/sector reindexing from the imported inertia/age equivalences. Nontrivial tangent eigenvalues are essential, so this is not the invariant of the coarse space alone.
acceptance: For a smooth scheme X the inertia has only age-zero identity and the invariant is ordinary E(X) or #X(Fq).

sources.match: The sector sum defines both invariants and explains independence of presentation and primitive generator.

uses.how: Realize each inertia sector by a fractional Lefschetz monomial.
Compare the twisted orbifold invariant on the PGL side with the ordinary SL invariant.

nodes.title: Gerbe-twisted stringy invariants
nodes.statement: For the same X, an étale μr-gerbe α and a fixed faithful embedding of μr into the coefficient field, import its transgression torsor Pα on IX. Define E_st(X,α)=Σ_Z E(Z,Pα|Z)(xy)^F(Z) by the specified character of the torsor total space, with centralizer invariants. Define #^α_st(X)=Σ_[z] q^F(z) Tr(Fr_z,Nα,z)/|Aut(z)|. All root embeddings, torsor-associated character conventions and age generators are transported together.
hypotheses: r is invertible and the finite-field roots required by the chosen sector presentation and μr-character are present.
Use geometric Frobenius, positive q^age, and the associated line local system Nα selecting the same character as the complex realization.
A μr-gerbe may be nonneutral even when its induced Gm-gerbe is neutral; transgression factors through that Gm-gerbe.

Whenever transgression is identified through the Gm image, impose the actual admissibility root condition μ_(r|Γ|) for the chosen finite quotient presentation on the base, as in the requested corrected Lemma2.9; over C it is automatic.
proofSteps: Import corrected action-groupoid descent and transgression from G-ETII, including the factorization through Gm-gerbes. Pull each sector torsor to its finite cover with Γ×μr-action.
Apply character-realizations to the torsor total space and append its age monomial. The stack trace formula supplies stabilizer denominators.
Use transgression pullback and inversion to prove functoriality, trivial-twist normalization and the inverse-sector/dual-local-system relation needed by the integral formula.
acceptance: For α=0 recover the untwisted invariants.
On a smooth scheme the identity-sector transgression is trivial, so these stringy invariants are ordinary even for a nonneutral μr-gerbe.

sources.match: The transgressed torsor supplies the sector coefficients for the twisted E-polynomial and weighted point count.

uses.how: Compare the sector trace with the complex conjugate of the Hasse-character integral.
The final mirror statement uses precisely these twisted coefficients.

nodes.title: Stringy counts determine E-polynomials
nodes.statement: Let R⊂C be of finite type, X_i=[Y_i/Γ_i] smooth finite abelian quotients over R, and α_i μr-gerbes. If their twisted stringy counts agree after every R→Fq at good residue characteristics and with compatible specified root/character choices, then E_st((X_1)_C,α_1)=E_st((X_2)_C,α_2). A common shrinking and finite étale cover is allowed, retaining the chosen complex fibres.
hypotheses: The root and character choices over residue fields are transported to the same complex convention; enlarge R to contain the finite needed roots.
All finite-field extensions remain in the hypothesis.
proofSteps: Put both presentations under Γ_1×Γ_2 and separate the finitely many connected inertia sectors. Realize transgression torsors as good Γ×μr-varieties.
Encode sector Z by its torsor total-space class times L^F(Z), using the faithful μr character and trivial centralizer character. The exponent is the age F, not the gerbe α.
Apply fractional-katz to the finite virtual difference; the compatible root/character conventions identify its E-realization with the required twisted stringy difference.
acceptance: For trivial groups and gerbes recover ordinary Katz comparison.
The expression uses the same finite set of age denominators on the two sides after common refinement.

sources.match: The theorem expresses stringy invariants as character realizations of fractional Lefschetz classes and then applies Katz comparison.

nodes.title: Arithmetic gerbes
nodes.statement: For f:U→V proper with geometrically connected fibres and a smooth commutative band B over V, a B-gerbe α on U is V-arithmetic when an étale covering {V_i→V} makes α|_(U×V V_i) neutral. For a field K this means geometric neutrality over K^s, with finite-presentation descent. Keep the band: arithmetic μr-neutrality is stronger than neutrality of its image in H²(U,Gm).
hypotheses: r is invertible when B=μr.

Use the imported algebraic stack/gerbe formalism; assume f_*Gm=Gm universally whenever a Picard or Hochschild–Serre statement below needs it, in particular for smooth proper geometrically connected fibres.
proofSteps: Define the local-neutrality property on the base étale site, using gerbes from R09.4.
Use the sheaf condition to transport along equivalences and base change; over a field descend a geometric neutralization to a finite separable extension.
Compare the μr and Gm images by extension of band, retaining the Kummer kernel Pic(U)/r.
acceptance: The neutral gerbe is arithmetic over any allowed base.
This is a property of the relative gerbe and its band, not an assertion that a global section exists.

sources.match: Arithmeticity is local neutrality after a cover of the base, not just local neutrality on U itself.

uses.how: Make the relative splitting stack a torsor and identify its Brauer obstruction.
Dual systems carry arithmetic gerbes on their regular torsor fibres.

nodes.title: Relative stacks of splittings
nodes.statement: For a V-arithmetic Gm-gerbe β on U, define the V-stack Split̃(U/V,β) by the groupoid of its neutralizations on U_T for T→V. Tensoring a neutralization by a line bundle gives an action of the relative Picard stack Pic̃(U/V), and this makes Split̃ a Pic̃-torsor. For a μr-gerbe α, use its μr-neutralizations and μr-rigidify to obtain Split_μr; it is a torsor under the rigidified relative μr-torsor sheaf, identified with Pic(U/V)[r] by the relative Kummer sequence.
hypotheses: f is proper, geometrically connected and cohomologically flat in degree zero in the chosen Picard representability interface.
r is invertible and the appropriate gerbe is V-arithmetic.
Rigidification is a sheaf construction; quotienting individual T-valued section sets is insufficient.
proofSteps: Use the imported Picard stack and gerbe maps. The sheaf of differences of any two neutralizations is a line bundle, or a μr-torsor with the band retained.
Arithmeticity makes the difference action locally nonempty, hence a torsor rather than just a pseudotorsor.
Apply R09.5/rigidification and its base-change theorem. On the base étale site, the Kummer map kills relative unit ambiguities and identifies the rigidified μr-torsor group with Pic[r].
acceptance: For Gm-neutralizations the difference is a line bundle; for μr-neutralizations it is a μr-torsor, equivalently a line bundle together with its rth-power trivialization. Retain the full difference groupoid before rigidification.

sources.match: The splitting groupoids carry the relative line-bundle action, and arithmeticity supplies local sections.

uses.how: Extend the Pic[r]-torsor to its Picτ principal component.
Identify neutralizations of a universal-family obstruction on a spectral fibre.

Forgetting the square trivialization before forming the groupoid loses this distinction.

nodes.title: The principal splitting torsor
nodes.statement: Let Picτ(U/V) be the inverse image in the relative Picard sheaf of the torsion subgroup of its geometric component group. For a V-arithmetic μr-gerbe α, define Split′(U/V,α)=Split_μr(U/V,α)×^(Pic(U/V)[r])Picτ(U/V). This is extension of structure group of a Pic[r]-torsor, not a chosen connected component of Split̃. Over an abelian-scheme torsor, identify Picτ=Pic0 with the dual abelian scheme.
hypotheses: Use the relative Picard representability and component-group interface imported from JacobianChallenge D and A2.
The map Pic[r]→Picτ is the natural inclusion and r is invertible.
Picτ=Pic0 is invoked only where proved; torsion in the Néron–Severi group can prevent it in general.
proofSteps: Form the contracted product as the fppf sheaf quotient of pairs (s,L) under (s,L)·t=(s·t,t⁻¹L). Import quotient representability and descent.
The residual Picτ action is locally simply transitive; descent gives the principal torsor. Base change and band/gerbe equivalences act on both factors.
For an abelian torsor, translation and the normalized Poincaré comparison identify Picτ with the dual abelian scheme; no origin of the torsor is chosen.
acceptance: A μr-neutralization gives a point of Split′; the reverse implication is not part of the construction.

sources.locator: §6.1, Definition 6.4 and the paragraph following it, p.566
sources.match: The principal splitting space is an extension from Pic[r] to Picτ, which can forget a constant gerbe obstruction.

uses.how: The opposite Hitchin fibre is this torsor under the dual Prym.
Its class gives the local Tate character and the Hausel–Thaddeus duality.

nodes.title: Principal splittings and constant Brauer classes
nodes.statement: For smooth proper geometrically connected X/K with H⁰(X_Ks,Gm)=(Ks)× and arithmetic μr-gerbe α, a K-point of Split′ implies that the induced Gm-class β lies in im(Br(K)→Br(X)). Use the middle-exact Hochschild–Serre edge sequence Pic(X)→Pic(X_Ks)^GK→Br(K)→Br(X)_K→H¹(GK,Pic(X_Ks))→H³(GK,(Ks)×). No injectivity of Br(K) or surjectivity to H¹ is assumed. A K-point of X gives injectivity, and H³=0 suffices for the right surjectivity.
hypotheses: All Picard sheaves and Galois modules are the imported geometric ones.
For more general proper X require explicitly the global-units hypothesis used by the edge sequence.
The conclusion concerns β, not neutrality of α as a μr-gerbe.
proofSteps: The cocycle description of principal-splitting sends β to the image of its Picτ-torsor class in H¹(K,Pic). A rational point kills that class.

Apply the exact low-degree sequence in SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/hochschild-serre-galois-covering (part3) with F=Gm, and the Picard identifications of SF.3/picard-brauer-sequence. Its exactness at Br(X)_K alone gives a constant Brauer class; no new geometric spectral sequence is needed.
Use pullback along a rational point only when present. The Kummer sequence explains why a possible Pic(X)/r residue prevents inferring μr-neutrality from β=0.
acceptance: For the real conic with no real point, the nonzero Hamilton Brauer class can map to zero, so the displayed sequence cannot begin with an unconditional injection.
For a local field with good integral point, evaluation of a constant class reduces to Br(O_F)=0 in local-brauer-splitting.

sources.locator: §6.1, equation (24) and Lemma 6.5, pp.565–566; correction E4
sources.match: Only the middle-exact part of Hochschild–Serre is needed for the constant-class conclusion.

nodes.title: Unitary and arithmetic principal splittings
nodes.statement: For smooth projective U→V over C, an arithmetic μr-gerbe α, and Picτ(U/V)=Pic0(U/V), identify the analytic space of Split′ with the manifold of flat unitary splittings of the corresponding unitary gerbe. The isomorphism is equivariant for the rank-one unitary-line/Pic0 comparison and compatible with pullback; it does not select a neutralization.
hypotheses: Retain Picτ=Pic0 and the smooth projective complex hypotheses.
The unitary gerbe and its flat splittings are imported from the rank-one extension requested of HodgeStructuresPartII H.1; that stage currently fixes a narrower determinant scope.
proofSteps: Apply the imported rank-one unitary-line/Pic0 equivalence to local neutralizations and their differences.
Both sides are obtained by extending the same Pic[r]-torsor of μr-neutralizations along Pic[r]→Pic0. Compare the descent cocycles, using arithmeticity.
The source only states the comparison as a remark; retain G-unitary until the analytic construction and family descent are supplied.
acceptance: For a neutral gerbe on an elliptic curve, both sides are its dual elliptic curve as real manifolds with their compatible complex structure.
This comparison is not required by the arithmetic integration proof; it is required for the stated compatibility with the original formulation.

sources.match: The remark identifies the principal contracted product with the unitary splitting convention used by Hausel–Thaddeus.

additionalSources.match: The proofs use the same extension of the finite splitting torsor by the dual Prym.

nodes.title: Abstract Hitchin systems
nodes.statement: An abstract Hitchin system over noetherian R consists of smooth A/R, a smooth admissible finite abelian quotient stack M/R, π:M→A with proper coarse map, and a smooth commutative A-group P acting relatively. Choose dense open A♦⊂A with P♦ an abelian scheme and a dense open M′⊂M which is a P-torsor over its image in A, contains M♦ and has complement of codimension at least two. The torsor need not be surjective over A. Use equidimensional components when writing q^dim M.
hypotheses: Admissible means the precise tame generically free quotient and root hypotheses of the imported Definition 4.10, not arbitrary finite inertia.
P is smooth along the zero section with locally free invariant differentials on the part used for gauge forms.
Properness belongs to the coarse map; M′ is an algebraic space, with no residual stabilizers.
proofSteps: Package the imported smooth stack, relative group action, dense opens and proper coarse morphism, with the stated geometric properties as proof obligations about those actual objects.
Use the torsor action to identify relative tangent bundles on M′ with the invariant tangent bundle of P.
Keep the codimension bound as a structural hypothesis: extension of a nowhere-zero top form and equality of orbifold/gauge measure use it.
acceptance: A smooth abelian scheme over A, viewed as its own torsor with no boundary, gives a system.

sources.match: The definition isolates the proper coarse fibration and its codimension-two torsor locus used by the measure argument.

uses.how: Transfer invariant relative top forms to the total space and integrate fibrewise.
Certify the SLn and PGLn examples after checking every open-locus and admissibility condition.

nodes.title: Dual Hitchin systems
nodes.statement: Take two abstract systems over the same A, arithmetic admissible μr-gerbes α_i, an étale isogeny φ:P1→P2 over all A, and ψ:(P1♦)∨≃P2♦ with ψφ∨=φψ∨ under biduality. Its geometric kernel degree over A♦ is a unit. Require Picτ=P_i∨ on regular fibres and equivariant isomorphisms Split′(M_i♦/A♦,α_i)≃M_(i′)♦ as P_(i′)♦-torsors. The local hypothesis sufficient for all comparisons is: whenever both fibres over b∈A(O_F)∩A♦(F) have F-points, both induced Gm-gerbes are neutral. The paper’s condition that both μr-gerbes are neutral iff both fibres have points is a stronger additional predicate; it implies the sufficient hypothesis, and its extra μr-neutrality assertion remains G-Kummer.
hypotheses: The local-field condition quantifies over each R→O_F and the indicated integral base points; retain the admissible root and prime-to-characteristic hypotheses.
Both systems have the same pure total dimension on the compared components, as supplied by their dual regular abelian fibres and common smooth base.
The isogeny is étale on all A where gauge forms are pulled back; generic étaleness alone is insufficient.
proofSteps: Use the imported dual abelian-scheme functor and Poincaré biduality to type the self-duality square. The splitting torsor acts by the opposite Prym, correcting E10.
Form the local evaluation condition on the induced Brauer classes, because the imported transgression and fα factor through Gm-gerbes.

Record the relationship to the literal μr splitting condition of Definition 6.9(d): the proof of the integral theorem only uses the displayed forward implication for Brauer neutrality. Do not use a point of Split′ to claim a μr-neutralization.
acceptance: Every pair satisfying the literal Definition 6.9, with its μr-neutrality proved, satisfies this sufficient formulation.
The main comparison theorems below are proved for the sufficient formulation; no converse between Brauer and μr neutrality is asserted.

sources.locator: §6.2, Definition 6.9 and Remark 6.10, pp.568–569; corrected torsor group E10; proof of Theorem 6.17, p.573
sources.match: The duality data supply the self-dual isogeny and the opposite splitting torsors. The local condition is stated at the Brauer strength actually used by the proof, with the stronger printed condition explicitly retained as a gate.

uses.how: Use the self-dual isogeny to equate local indices and fibre volumes.
The opposite splitting torsor class gives a nontrivial Tate character when the opposite fibre has no point; Brauer neutrality gives phase 1 when both have points.

nodes.title: Compatible gauge forms
nodes.statement: Zariski locally on A choose a top form η generating Ω^top_(A/O_F) and a generator θ2 of the invariant relative top forms of P2/A. Set θ1=φ*θ2. Transfer θi to the torsor locus M_i′ and form ωi=π_i*η∧θi there. Extend uniquely across its codimension-at-least-two complement to a nowhere-vanishing top form on the smooth stack M_i. Its absolute-value measure on the generically free coarse locus is the imported orbifold measure. These local forms glue as measures; no global triviality of the canonical bundle on all of A is assumed.
hypotheses: The zero-section determinant line of the invariant relative differentials is trivialized on the chosen base neighborhood. A group scheme gives that line by pullback, not a global generator without shrinking.
φ is étale over this neighborhood, so pullback preserves a generator integrally.
Smoothness/normality and a codimension-two complement are required for invertible-sheaf Hartogs extension.
proofSteps: Import the invariant differential identification for a smooth group torsor from G-ETII, including independence of its trivialization.
Apply pullback and the determinant exact sequence for the smooth torsor map to construct the nowhere-zero form on M′.
Use the smooth-stack Hartogs interface requested of R09.4 to extend the section and its inverse trivialization across codimension two.
Use the imported orbifold/gauge comparison on the free locus. Changes of compatible integral generators multiply absolute values by units of norm one, giving the same measure.
acceptance: The exceptional divisor after blowing up a smooth point blocks the extension argument for the old torsor locus.
For the product elliptic system, η=dt and a fixed invariant elliptic differential give the product measure.

sources.match: Compatible invariant top forms descend to torsors and extend across the small boundary to compute the orbifold measure.

uses.how: Fix the normalization θ1=φ*θ2 in the change-of-variables calculation.
Fubini integrates equal fibre characters against a common base gauge measure.

nodes.title: Twisted counts as local integrals
nodes.statement: For an admissible smooth finite abelian quotient M/O_F of pure relative dimension m and an admissible μr-gerbe α, #^α_st(M_k)/q^m=∫_(M(O_F)^natural) conjugate(fα)dμ_orb, where fα(x)=exp(2πi inv(x*β)) for the induced Brauer gerbe β and the fixed normalized embeddings. Here M(O_F)^natural means coarse integral points whose generic point is in the free locus.
hypotheses: Use the precise root, tame and admissible-gerbe assumptions exported by G-ETII.
The Hasse/transgression identification must include inherited source gates E15 and E16; no use of the published comparison bypasses those gates.
proofSteps: Apply the imported specialization-sector measure formula q^(−w)/|Aut| and the Hasse/transgression theorem to integrate each constant transgression phase.
Reindex γ by γ⁻¹. The age identity w(γ)=m−F(γ⁻¹) and dualization of the inertia local system produce complex conjugation of fα.
Sum all rational sector classes. The normalization is q^m, not the base dimension or a coarse unweighted count.
acceptance: For a smooth scheme with trivial gerbe, recover Weil’s volume formula #M(k)/q^m.
For a primitive cube-root phase, omitting the conjugation gives its inverse and fails the fixed convention.

sources.match: The stringy count equals the conjugate gerbe-character integral after dimension normalization and inertia inversion.

nodes.title: Equal volumes of dual regular fibres
nodes.statement: For a dual pair and b∈A(O_F)∩A♦(F), if both regular fibres have F-points, then ∫_(M1,b(F))|θ1,b|=∫_(M2,b(F))|θ2,b|. The forms are exactly those of compatible-gauge-forms.
hypotheses: The fibres P_i,b are dual abelian varieties and the isogeny is self-dual of prime-to-residue-characteristic degree.
The local index input is needed for F=k((t)) as well as characteristic-zero local fields. The existing R02.4 node only states characteristic zero; G-local records this extension.
proofSteps: Trivialize each torsor at an F-point; invariant forms make the integral independent of that point.
Change variables under φ: the integral on P1 is |ker φ(F)| times the integral on φ(P1(F)) with θ2. Translation invariance multiplies the latter by |P2(F)/φP1(F)| to give the full P2 volume.
Apply the self-dual isogeny index theorem, after its prime-to-characteristic equal-characteristic extension G-local, to identify these two finite factors.
acceptance: For φ=id on a self-dual elliptic product, both finite factors are 1.
For φ=[n] on a principally polarized elliptic curve at n prime to p, the finite kernel and cokernel have the same order even when not every geometric n-torsion point is F-rational.

sources.match: The key lemma converts the self-dual local index formula into equality of compatible fibre volumes.

nodes.title: Fibrewise gerbe-character integrals
nodes.statement: For every b∈A(O_F)∩A♦(F) in a dual pair, ∫_(M1,b(F)) fα1|θ1,b|=∫_(M2,b(F)) fα2|θ2,b|, with the empty-domain integral equal to zero.
hypotheses: Use the sufficient local Brauer condition in dual-hitchin-pair and the imported Tate-character formula for arithmetic gerbes.
Retain G-ETII and G-local, including the corrected μr-gerbe version of the Ext input.
proofSteps: If both point sets are empty, both integrals vanish.

If exactly one is nonempty, identify that torsor with its abelian group. By the imported Lemma 6.7 its phase is a constant root of unity times the Tate character of the nonzero opposite torsor class. Local Tate nondegeneracy makes the character nontrivial, and Haar translation gives integral zero.
If both are nonempty, the sufficient local condition makes both underlying Brauer gerbes neutral. Their evaluation functions are 1 by the imported factorization, and equal-fibre-volumes applies.
The symmetric one-empty case is identical with the roles exchanged. Conjugating the equality supplies the convention used in twisted-integral.
acceptance: A nontrivial character has integral zero even after multiplication by a constant root of unity.
The both-nonempty case requires Brauer triviality, not just constancy with an unknown phase.

sources.match: The four cases reduce mirror integration either to Tate-character cancellation or to the key volume lemma.

nodes.title: Fibrewise arithmetic mirror symmetry
nodes.statement: For a dual pair over finite k=Fq, the twisted stringy counts agree. More precisely, for every a∈A(k) and every finite extension k_m/k, the alternating geometric-Frobenius trace of the inertia-fibre compact cohomology with coefficients Nα1⊗Qbarℓ(−F1) equals that for Nα2⊗Qbarℓ(−F2), over a after base change to k_m. The rational age twist is made on each connected sector with a compatible finite denominator; it is not a fractional cohomological shift.
hypotheses: The proper coarse maps and finite inertia justify the required proper/compact fibre trace comparison from G-ETII.
Both total dimensions agree. The finite extension inherits or enlarges the chosen roots consistently.
proofSteps: Base change the finite-field pair to O_F=k[[t]], so equal-characteristic local duality is genuinely necessary. Fix a residue base point a.
The stack trace formula and twisted-integral identify the normalized inertia-fibre trace with the integral over the reduction tube above a, with the required conjugate phase.
Use compatible-gauge-forms and Fubini. Remove the complement of A♦(F), which is a null set for the smooth base measure, then apply local-mirror-integral on every remaining fibre.
The common q^dim M normalization gives equality of the unnormalized traces. Repeat over every finite extension and sum over a for the global stringy count.
acceptance: The conclusion is an equality of alternating traces for all Frobenius powers. It does not itself separate individual cohomological degrees or detect extension classes.
For the neutral elliptic product it reduces to the same ordinary count on both sides above each a.

sources.match: The arithmetic theorem is fibrewise and follows by integration over residue tubes, with stack trace and Fubini.

nodes.title: Complex mirror symmetry for abstract systems
nodes.statement: For a dual pair over a finite-type subalgebra R⊂C, E_st((M1)_C,α1)=E_st((M2)_C,α2), in the rational-bidegree realization with the fixed character conventions.
hypotheses: Spread all duality data, finite denominators, admissible roots and the sufficient local condition over a common model; perform only the allowed base changes preserving the system data.
The proof uses the explicit supplier gates of stringy-comparison and arithmetic-mirror.
proofSteps: Apply arithmetic-mirror after each good finite-field specialization of the common model, including every finite extension.
Apply stringy-comparison to that equality of twisted counts.

nodes.title: Stable trace-free fixed-determinant moduli
nodes.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically connected genus-g curve X/S over a noetherian base, a line bundle D, n≥1 invertible on S and L of degree d with gcd(n,d)=1, form the stable locus in the imported D-Higgs stack, impose Trθ=0 and an isomorphism det E≃L, and μn-rigidify its scalar stabilizers. Denote the resulting finite-type separated coarse algebraic space by M_SL^L; in the source’s projective-curve setting prove that it is a quasiprojective scheme. Stability means every proper nonzero θ-invariant saturated subbundle has smaller slope. The trace-free characteristic-coefficient map lands in A=⊕_(i=2)^n f_*D^i when these sheaves satisfy the stated locally-free/base-change interface.
hypotheses: The basic Higgs stack, characteristic polynomial and spectral carrier are imports from ET.2b, not new definitions here. Its existing node is over finite fields; the relative noetherian-family adapter is requested explicitly.
For D=ω import the general stable GLn carrier and its stability from CB.7; extend those notions to this D-twist and fixed determinant, retaining their meaning.
Fixed determinant with its isomorphism has μn scalar stabilizers; the unfixed-determinant stable stack has Gm stabilizers. Do not rigidify the former by Gm.
Use projective curves or a verified relative polarization where the moduli construction needs one.
proofSteps: Extend the imported carrier by descent to the specified family bases, using current upstream AlgebraicVectorBundles for finite locally free sheaves, tensor products and determinants.

Use the existing slope/stability interface, with D replacing ω, and the imported bounded Quot/parameter-space machinery. The required stable-Higgs GIT/adequate-quotient interface is G-moduli; R09.1–2 alone do not assert this quotient.

Form the fixed-determinant and trace-zero fibre, then apply the existing rigidification and its base-change theorem. Establish finite type and separatedness; prove quasiprojectivity in the selected projective family setting.
Use characteristic coefficients rather than power traces, so no division by 2,…,n is hidden. Record the actual H⁰(D^i) base-change identification.
acceptance: Over an algebraically closed field a stable fixed-determinant object has exactly μn automorphisms before rigidification and none afterwards.

nodes.title: Smoothness of stable fixed-determinant moduli
nodes.statement: Under the preceding moduli hypotheses, suppose D⊗ω_X/S⁻¹ has positive degree on every geometric fibre or is trivial. Then M_SL^L is smooth over S. At a geometric point its deformation complex is End0(E)→End0(E)⊗D, δ(u)=θu−(u⊗1)θ, in degrees 0 and 1; H⁰ gives infinitesimal automorphisms, H¹ the tangent space and H² the obstruction. Stability and n invertible kill H⁰, and Serre duality and the D condition kill H². Its relative dimension on nonempty fibres is (n²−1)deg D.
hypotheses: The degree and base-change hypotheses are fibrewise and the moduli deformation interface is G-moduli.
For D=ω the degree formula is 2(n²−1)(g−1); a negative value signals emptiness, not a negative-dimensional smooth scheme.
When the residue characteristic divides n, scalar endomorphisms may have trace zero, so this argument is not applicable.
proofSteps: Use the imported deformation theory of Higgs pairs and the trace/determinant differential to obtain the End0 complex, with an explicit cohomological indexing convention.
A stable Higgs endomorphism is scalar. Since n is a unit its trace-zero part vanishes.
Serre duality identifies H² with trace-free Higgs maps E→E⊗ωD⁻¹. Negative degree gives vanishing by stability; for D=ω it reduces to the same trace-free endomorphism vanishing.

Apply the infinitesimal lifting criterion to the actual moduli stack and rigidification; use Riemann–Roch for the stated dimension and verify relative smoothness by the chosen finite-presentation criterion.
acceptance: For n=1 the complex is zero and the dimension is zero.
In characteristic p dividing n, id_E∈End0(E) demonstrates why the n-unit hypothesis cannot be removed.

nodes.title: PGLn moduli as a finite quotient
nodes.statement: Let Γ=J_X[n], finite étale of rank n^(2g) when n is invertible. Tensoring E by an n-torsion line defines its action on M_SL^L. Define the stable PGLn stack of degree class d mod n by M_PGL^d=[M_SL^L/Γ], and identify it with the intended geometric stable PGL moduli by étale-local lifts and descent. The quotient is independent of L after the corresponding determinant twists; its coarse quotient and the stack are kept distinct.
hypotheses: After a finite étale base change Γ may be made constant; arithmetic formulas explicitly use this choice.
All n-torsion actions and quotients are sheaf/stack actions, including the determinant trivialization coherence before rigidification.
This construction does not assert generic freeness until regular-hitchin-certificate verifies it.
proofSteps: Use tensor functoriality of the existing Higgs carrier and det(E⊗N)=det(E)N^n to define Γ action on the rigidified space.
Use quotient-stack descent from R09.4. A local lift of a PGL bundle differs from another by tensoring a line bundle; normalize determinants using the n-power map and descend.
Construct the coarse quotient separately with the imported finite quotient interface. The residual fixed-point stabilizers remain in the PGL stack.
acceptance: The Γ action preserves the Hitchin map because tensoring a line preserves the characteristic polynomial.

nodes.statement: For gcd(n,d)=1 in the smooth projective curve and D setting above, the stable GLn and fixed-determinant trace-free SLn Hitchin morphisms are proper; so is the PGL coarse Hitchin map. Properness is not asserted of the nonproper total Higgs space over the ground field.

The source cites Nitsure for D-twisted semistable Higgs properness and Faltings for the relative setting; their proof interfaces remain G-moduli.
In the canonical GLn case the precise existing CB.7/higgs-moduli statement is imported rather than planned again.
proofSteps: Import the semistable Hitchin properness theorem for the selected family bases through G-moduli. Coprimality identifies stable and semistable rank-degree classes.
The determinant and trace conditions form the closed relative fibre needed for properness of SL.

nodes.title: Determinant change and Γ-twists
nodes.statement: For N a line bundle, tensoring gives M_SL^L≃M_SL^(L N^n) over the Hitchin base. If L1,L2 have the same degree, the n-root sheaf T of L2 L1⁻¹ on the base is a Γ-torsor; contracting M_SL^L1 with T gives M_SL^L2, with the tensor action and descent conventions fixed. Over finite k use the Kummer identification J_X(k)/nJ_X(k)≃H¹(k,Γ), which needs Lang’s vanishing H¹(k,J_X)=0.
hypotheses: For a family the root object is an étale sheaf torsor, not an asserted global line bundle.

For the arithmetic ν-labeling used in §7.5, set ν=δ(L1 L2⁻¹) as in the source, so its geometric Frobenius acts as ν⁻¹Fr. This is the inverse of the positive-root cocycle if that cocycle was used for T.

Choose local nth roots of L2 L1⁻¹ in the relative Jacobian and compute their Γ transition cocycle. The same cocycle glues the tensor maps.

nodes.title: Stable spectral fibres as norm preimages
nodes.statement: On the regular locus with smooth connected spectral cover π:Y_a→X of degree n, set M=det(π_*O_Y). The spectral correspondence identifies the SL Hitchin fibre with P_a^L=Nm_π⁻¹(L M⁻¹), a torsor under P_a^0=ker(Nm:J_Y→J_X) when that kernel is connected. The norm is Nm(B)=det(π_*B)M⁻¹. The PGL fibre is the corresponding quotient by Γ. The determinant correction is L M⁻¹, never L M.
hypotheses: Use the imported spectral correspondence with a verified relative-base-change version, and the stable regular spectral locus.
Smoothness of Y alone is not assumed to imply connectedness, stability or nonemptiness; these are established in regular-hitchin-certificate or remain G-lowgenus.
For the monic spectral algebra, π_*O_Y=⊕_(j=0)^(n−1) D^(−j), so M=D^(−n(n−1)/2), independent of the Hitchin parameter.
proofSteps: Use the ET.2b spectral module equivalence and its relative extension requested in G-moduli. A spectral line B pushes forward to E with det E=Nm(B)M.
Solve det E=L to obtain the displayed inverse-M norm target; retain the determinant-isomorphism and rigidification comparisons between the spectral Picard stack and its fibre space.
Use the relative norm map on Jacobians from the A2 request, and identify its kernel action with the imported Picard action. Quotient by Γ for PGL.
acceptance: For n=1, M=O and Nm=id, so the fixed-L fibre is a point.
For n=2, M=D⁻¹ and the norm target is L D; the opposite sign would give L D⁻¹.

nodes.title: The PGLn Prym group
nodes.statement: For the spectral family and its norm-kernel group P_SL acting on the stable SL fibration, define P_PGL=P_SL/Γ using the pullback inclusion π*:J_X[n]→P_SL. On the smooth connected regular locus this identifies with J_Y/π*J_X. The map φ:P_SL→P_PGL has kernel Γ and is a finite étale isogeny when n is a unit and the pullback inclusion has been verified.
hypotheses: The global norm-Picard family over A, including singular spectral fibres, is an imported relative Picard-action interface; its extension is explicitly requested from ET.2b and A2.

Check π* injectivity and connected norm kernel on the regular locus. For deg D>0, the negative-degree spectral summands give the required pullback injectivity; low-degree exceptions remain G-lowgenus.
No general construction of abelian quotients or duals is duplicated: A3 supplies those on A♦.
proofSteps: Use the norm identity Nm(π*N)=N^n to map Γ into the SL norm kernel; prove injectivity under the selected spectral hypotheses.
Form the fppf quotient, importing finite quotient representability and A3 on regular abelian fibres.

The n-power map on J_X is fppf-surjective; use it to identify the quotient of the norm kernel by Γ with J_Y/π*J_X on A♦. Extend the specified group/action globally by the imported Picard-family construction, with its exact smoothness and étaleness obligations.

The comparison identifies the actual evaluation/Poincaré pairings and the kernel Weil pairing, not merely the dimensions of two abelian schemes.

nodes.title: Regular locus and abstract-system certificates
nodes.statement: Construct the specified regular open and torsor loci for the stable SLn and PGLn fibrations, prove smoothness of the relevant Picard group families, properness of the coarse maps, generic freeness/admissibility of the quotient, and codim(M∖M′)≥2, and thereby certify Definition 6.8. On the geometric range where smooth spectral curves are connected and the stable regular locus is nonempty, the source’s smooth-spectral locus supplies A♦. The theorem’s full genus range requires a separate verification; it is not silently reduced to g≥2.
hypotheses: Use the actual stable moduli and characteristic/root hypotheses established in this layer.
The finite-field ET.2b anisotropic properness and δ-codimension theorem do not automatically give this noetherian-family stable certificate.

For g=1,D=ω=O,n>1 a generic trace-free characteristic polynomial has distinct constant roots. Its global projectors split any Higgs bundle into eigenbundles; one has slope at least the total slope. Hence the stable generic fibre is empty. Smooth spectral therefore cannot be treated as automatically connected with nonempty stable fibres.
proofSteps: Use the relative spectral and Picard action interfaces to identify the regular group torsors; compare the selected opens with the source’s regular locus.
Prove the complement codimension and the quotient generic-freeness statement in the actual stable spaces, importing the needed Ngô regular-centralizer input through ET.2b rather than replanning it.

For deg D>0, verify spectral pullback injectivity by the decomposition π_*O_Y and the vanishing of sections of negative-degree line bundles. Check connectedness and dense regular fibres in the precise range used.

Retain G-lowgenus for the remaining low-degree/genus cases and for a primary-proof-level verification of the codimension certificate. Direct low-genus mirror calculations can replace the abstract certificate, but are not claimed here.

Test the elliptic canonical-twist generic polynomial before asserting nonempty smooth connected stable spectral fibres.

nodes.title: Spectral torsor products, powers and periods
nodes.statement: With P_a^L=Nm⁻¹(L M⁻¹), contracted product gives P^L·P^L′≃P^(L L′ M⁻¹), and for every integer e, (P^L)^e≃P^(L^e M^(1−e)). Tensoring by π*Q gives P^L≃P^(L Q^n). The class of an SL spectral torsor is n-torsion, since the nth power norm target is realized by π*(L M⁻¹). For GL spectral Picard torsors, their period divides n when Pic¹(X)(F) contains an actual degree-one line bundle; its pullback has degree n.
hypotheses: All equalities are equivariant isomorphisms of torsors under the same regular Prym or Jacobian, not equalities of chosen points.
For GL period arguments the degree-one line bundle is established over finite residue fields by Picard/Lang/Brauer inputs and lifted in the smooth Picard family before passing to F.
Use integer powers in the commutative torsor group, including inverse torsors; the e=0 result is P^M, the norm-identity torsor.
proofSteps: Multiply norm targets using the norm homomorphism and solve again for the determinant label. This gives the inverse-M correction in the product formula.
Induct for nonnegative powers, use inverse torsors for negative powers, and compare pullback line bundles via Nm(π*Q)=Q^n.
Exhibit π*(L M⁻¹) in the nth contracted power to prove the SL period bound. For GL, exhibit the degree-n pullback line and use the degree torsor law.
Record M=D^(−n(n−1)/2) as a single line on X independent of a; the correction N is therefore uniform over all regular spectral parameters.
acceptance: At e=1 the determinant label is L; at e=0 it is M and the norm target is O.
For n=2, (P^L)^2=P^(L²D), not P^(L²D⁻¹).
A class t killed by n is zero iff et is zero whenever gcd(e,n)=1, by Bézout; coprimality with d alone would be irrelevant.

nodes.title: GLn coprime-degree point counts
nodes.statement: Let X/Fq be smooth projective geometrically connected, Dω⁻¹ of positive even degree or trivial, n,d>0 coprime, p∤nd, μ_(n^(2g))⊂Fq, and e coprime to n and p. Then #M_GL^d(Fq)=#M_GL^e(Fq). This is the D-twisted comparison by local integration; the canonical GL carrier and the separate all-degree counting theorem of CB are imports.
hypotheses: All stable moduli and properness hypotheses from TMS.3 are retained.
The generic spectral Picard torsor period bound uses an actual degree-one line bundle on X, available over finite fields and liftable over the chosen smooth Picard model.
The source’s proof writes an irrelevant coprimality with d; the torsor-class argument uses gcd(d,n)=gcd(e,n)=1.
proofSteps: Lift the curve and finite list of line bundles to a complete unramified characteristic-zero discrete valuation ring with residue field Fq. Smoothness of the curve and H²=0 give the curve/Picard lifting interface requested in G-moduli.

On the regular spectral base the degree-d fibre is the dth power of the degree-one Jacobian torsor, whose class is killed by n. Bézout makes its triviality independent of d in the unit classes modulo n.

Choose common invariant relative forms and a base form, remove the measure-zero singular base, and integrate fibre volumes. Nonempty Jacobian torsors have the same translation-invariant volume; empty ones contribute zero.
Use Weil’s smooth-model formula and equal dimensions to return to point counts. G-lowgenus retains the omitted boundary cases of the regular-certificate argument.
acceptance: For n=1 the space is Pic^d(X)×H⁰(D); Pic^d is a Jacobian torsor with a finite-field point and all degrees have the same count.
The period argument must use e prime to n, not e prime to d.

nodes.statement: Under the source’s assumptions p>n, gcd(n,d)=1, μ_(n^(2g))⊂Fq and Dω⁻¹ of positive even degree or trivial, there is a line bundle N of degree zero such that, for every integer e prime to n, #M_SL^L(Fq)=#M_SL^(L^e N^(e−1))(Fq). Set M=D^(−n(n−1)/2). Choose Q with n deg Q=deg M and take the corrected N=M⁻¹Q^n. The choices can be made over the residue curve and lifted uniformly before integration.

Existence of Q over a finite field follows from a Picard degree component having a rational point and Br(Fq)=0, not from the integer degree calculation alone.
The line N is independent of the spectral parameter a.

The corrected eth power is P^(L^e M^(1−e)). Tensor by π*Q^(e−1) to replace that label by L^e(M⁻¹Q^n)^(e−1).
Integrate the resulting identical triviality indicators against the same invariant Prym volume and base form.
Apply Weil’s formula to the equal total volumes. The printed sign in N and in the torsor power is corrected throughout.

At e=1 the right determinant is L, giving the identity comparison.

nodes.title: Betti and Hodge numbers in coprime degree
nodes.statement: Over C with the same curve, D and coprimality hypotheses, the Betti numbers and the cohomologically graded Hodge numbers of M_GL^d and M_SL^L are independent of the coprime degree. Within a fixed degree, changing L is realized by tensoring an nth root over C. Across coprime degree classes, combine the arithmetic comparisons with purity; equality of E-polynomials alone is insufficient.
hypotheses: The compact-support geometric mixed Hodge realization and comparison are G-MHS.

Import the canonical GL ℓ-adic purity node CB.9/higgs-purity. Its extension to D-twisted and fixed-determinant geometric Hodge cohomology is the explicit G-Higgs-purity contract, not an existing conclusion of that node.
Purity must state weight k for H_c^k, so the coefficient with p+q=k determines the sign and the cohomological degree.
proofSteps: For two degrees d₁,d₂ prime to n choose e with ed₁≡d₂ mod n. Over C fix Q of degree deg M/n and N=M⁻¹Q^n. Choose a line of degree (d₂−ed₁)/n and an nth root in Pic0 so that the second determinant differs from L₁^eN^(e−1) by an actual nth power. Spread these fixed choices simultaneously. Apply the SL count comparison and determinant twisting after all good reductions; use the GL comparison for GL. Katz then gives equal E-polynomials. This does not presume determinant independence of finite-field counts.

nodes.title: Hausel–Thaddeus gerbes
nodes.statement: The stable fixed-determinant Higgs stack over its μn-rigidified space defines a μn-gerbe α_SL,L, the obstruction to a universal fixed-determinant family. Construct a coherent Γ-equivariant structure and descend it to α_PGL,L on [M_SL^L/Γ]. For e prime to n choose a with ad≡e mod n and put L′=L^a; the PGL degree is e mod n. The comparison uses α_SL,L^e and α_PGL,L′^d.
hypotheses: n is invertible, Γ=J_X[n] is constant after the chosen finite étale base change, and μ_(n|Γ|)=μ_(n^(2g+1)) is constant.
Equivariance is action-groupoid descent with pullback-twisted multiplication of the associated line torsors; an ordinary group extension with ignored base action is not a substitute.
L′ need only have degree congruent to e modulo n; the quotient identifies the degree-class component.
proofSteps: Use stable-fixed-determinant and the imported μn-rigidification theorem to obtain the gerbe and its universal-family interpretation.

Build tensor action and the scalar coherence on the gerbe. Use étale-local curve sections and normalized Poincaré lines to define the descent isomorphisms; prove their cocycle and independence of auxiliary choices. This arithmetic-family verification is G-HT-descent.
Apply the corrected descent/transgression interface from G-ETII to form the quotient gerbe. Take its indicated powers with the band fixed.

nodes.title: Duality of the gerbe splitting torsors
nodes.statement: On the common connected regular spectral locus, the two powered gerbes are arithmetic and there are canonical equivariant identifications Split′((M_SL^L)♦/A♦,α_SL,L^e)≃(M_PGL^e)♦ and Split′((M_PGL^e)♦/A♦,α_PGL,L′^d)≃(M_SL^L)♦, under the opposite PGL and SL Prym actions respectively.
hypotheses: The integer choices and root/admissibility data are those of hausel-thaddeus-gerbes.
The dual Prym and norm conventions are exactly TMS.3’s corrected ones.
The complex HT03 propositions use unitary language. Their contracted-product proofs must be made algebraic and descended over the noetherian base; this is G-HT-descent.
proofSteps: On a smooth spectral fibre use a universal line normalized at a local section to identify the finite μn-neutralization torsor, then extend its action by the dual Prym.

Use the normalized Poincaré bundle and theorem of the cube to compare the two torsors and their degree powers, following HT03 Propositions 3.2 and 3.6. Verify the opposite action and tensor-product coherence.
Descend the local constructions, including changes of normalization section, and prove base-change compatibility over the arithmetic model; a topological isomorphism over C is not sufficient here.

Verify arithmetic μn-neutrality separately by an étale-local spectral universal family with its actual determinant normalization. A local section of Split′ alone does not imply μn-neutrality. Construct the displayed torsor identifications only after this verification; G-HT-descent includes that proof obligation.

Check each equivalence is equivariant under P_i′, rather than merely an isomorphism of underlying spaces.

nodes.title: Local Brauer splitting of the powered gerbes
nodes.statement: Over O_F with the prescribed roots, if the two regular fibres above b∈A(O_F)∩A♦(F) have F-points, both powered gerbes have neutral induced Gm-gerbes on those fibres. Consequently both Hasse-character functions are 1 there. This is the local condition actually needed by the integral proof. The source’s stronger μn-neutrality equivalence is retained separately as G-Kummer.
hypotheses: Use the smooth stable SL space, proper Hitchin map, and Brauer(O_F)=0 for a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field.
For the PGL side construct an integral point as the image of an integral SL point in the appropriate degree, rather than assume every coarse stack point lifts integrally.
proofSteps: The opposite regular fibre point and ht-splitting-duality give a point of Split′. Apply constant-brauer to make the underlying Gm-gerbe a constant class along each fibre.
An SL F-point over an integral Hitchin parameter extends to O_F by properness. Evaluation of its gerbe gives a class in Br(O_F)=0; the constant Brauer class is therefore zero.

Use spectral-torsor-calculus and the prime-to-n degree powers to obtain an SL point of the degree needed for the PGL fibre. Extend it integrally and take its image in the PGL quotient to evaluate the other constant class.
Apply the imported factorization of transgression/Hasse evaluation through Gm-gerbes. Do not erase a possible Pic/r Kummer residue of the original μn-gerbe.
acceptance: A constant nonzero Brauer phase would make fα a nontrivial constant; Br(O_F)=0 is the step excluding it.
The proof does not claim that Br=0 implies H²(μn)=0 on the entire positive-dimensional fibre.

sources.match: The proof establishes the constant Brauer class and kills it by an integral point. The plan separates this valid consequence from the stronger band-neutrality wording.

nodes.statement: Combine the two stable Hitchin fibrations, their Prym groups, and α_SL,L^e and α_PGL,L′^d into a dual pair in the sufficient local-Brauer sense of TMS.2. The isogeny is P_SL→P_SL/Γ, its regular duality is the Prym Poincaré comparison, the principal splittings are the opposite fibres, and local Brauer neutrality holds when both have points. The full low-genus range and the literal μn-neutrality variant remain the recorded gates.
hypotheses: Use the common A♦ and every codimension/admissibility condition in regular-hitchin-certificate.
n and the quotient kernel degree are units. Γ and μ_(n^(2g+1)) are constant on the chosen model.
proofSteps: Apply regular-hitchin-certificate for the abstract-system data, without replacing it by a generic properness assertion.
Use pgl-prym for the globally étale isogeny and prym-duality for the self-duality square.
Apply ht-splitting-duality and local-brauer-splitting. The root hypothesis n|Γ| makes the gerbes admissible through G-ETII.
Distinguish the sufficient pair that has been constructed from the extra literal μn-neutrality claim; the latter is not needed to deduce the main invariant equality.

A non-generically-free low-genus quotient is not accepted as an admissible abstract system by this assembly alone.

nodes.title: SLn/PGLn topological mirror symmetry
nodes.statement: Let X/k be smooth projective geometrically connected of genus g, Dω⁻¹ have strictly positive even degree or be trivial, n≥1, gcd(n,d)=gcd(n,e)=1, L∈Pic^d(X), and μ_(n^(2g+1))⊂k. Choose L′=L^a with ad≡e mod n. Over C the target is E(M_SL^L;x,y)=E_st(M_PGL^e,α_PGL,L′^d;x,y). Over k=Fq of characteristic p>n the target is #M_SL^L(k)=#^α_st(M_PGL^e). The same root/gerbe conventions are used on both sides.
hypotheses: The full stated genus range is retained as a target. The abstract-system proof is established only once G-lowgenus verifies its geometric certificate or supplies separate low-genus calculations.
All generic integration, realization and arithmetic gerbe descent gates in the supplying nodes remain visible.
proofSteps: Spread the complex data to finite-type R⊂C with n inverted and the required finite roots; make Γ constant by a finite étale cover preserving the chosen complex point.
Apply sl-pgl-dual-pair, then abstract-mirror or arithmetic-mirror. This uses the sufficient local Brauer version whose proof was supplied in TMS.2.
On the smooth SL scheme only the identity inertia sector remains; its age is zero and transgression is trivial, so the twisted stringy invariant there is the ordinary one.
For every low-genus/degree component where the abstract certificate is not verified, leave G-lowgenus open rather than silently changing the theorem’s hypotheses.
acceptance: At n=1 both moduli and both invariants are 1.
For n=2,g=2,D=ω, use Γ of order 16 and the root order 32; the result specializes to the rank-two case independently checked by Hausel–Thaddeus.
The finite-field version requires the stated roots and p>n; no unsupported small-characteristic extension is asserted.

sources.match: The main theorem applies the abstract comparison to the dual SLn/PGLn data and simplifies the smooth SL side.

nodes.title: Canonical-twist Hodge numbers
nodes.statement: For D=ω over C under the main theorem’s hypotheses, the compact stringy Hodge numbers of (M_PGL^e,α_PGL,L′^d) equal the compact Hodge numbers of M_SL^L. On an inertia component Z of age a, the stringy summand H_c^k(Z,Nα) has stringy degree k+2a and Hodge bidegree (p+a,q+a). Purity must identify its weight with k before this shift, so the shifted weight equals the stringy degree.
hypotheses: The finite-monodromy local-system MHS is constructed through the torsor total-space character projector in G-MHS.
Use G-Higgs-purity for canonical fixed-determinant spaces and their finite-order fixed loci; the generic CB.9 GL assertion alone does not state this sector version.
The result uses age-shifted rational indices; it does not assert equality of unshifted individual sector cohomologies.

For D=ω the Γ-action preserves the holomorphic symplectic form. Its nontrivial tangent eigenvalues pair as ζ^b and ζ^(n−b), so every sector has integral age a=codim(Z)/2. The shift 2a is even and preserves the alternating sign.
proofSteps: Apply main-mirror for equality of E-polynomials.
Use the requested semiprojective purity statement on SL and on the finite-order fixed-locus torsor covers, with the character projector and finite quotient invariants. Track compact-support degrees.

Use symplectic eigenvalue pairing to prove a is integral. Purity gives weight k before the shift and weight k+2a afterwards. Since 2a is even, the sign (−1)^k agrees with (−1)^(k+2a); p+q=k+2a therefore separates the signs. Extract each Hodge number coefficientwise.
acceptance: For n=1 the only nonzero compact Hodge number is h_c^(0,0)=1.
A mixed sector without purity cannot be read degree by degree from its alternating E-polynomial.
A nonsymplectic sector of age 1/2 cannot use this parity argument; the canonical-twist hypothesis is essential to this proof.

sources.locator: §7.4, Corollary 7.22 and proof, p.589; HT03 §6, numbered pp.17–18
sources.match: The Hodge-number conclusion requires the stated purity of the canonical-twist and twisted-sector cohomology.

nodes.title: The justified fibrewise virtual comparison
nodes.statement: For every a∈A(Fq) in the main finite-field setting and every m≥1, the alternating trace of Fr^m on the SL Hitchin fibre equals that on the twisted PGL inertia fibre with the negative age Tate twists. Consequently their alternating classes agree in the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional continuous Qbarℓ-representations of Gal(Fq), after a common finite coefficient extension for the finite set of fractional twists. This is a virtual equality; individual degrees and nonsplit extensions are not identified.
hypotheses: Use all extension-field identities of arithmetic-mirror, with the compatible mth Frobenius powers of the same finite-denominator Tate roots.
The cohomological complexes have finite-dimensional bounded cohomology from proper coarse fibres and the imported tame-stack formalism.
proofSteps: Apply arithmetic-mirror to the SL/PGL pair above a over every finite extension.
Collect even and odd cohomology as virtual continuous representations with the fixed negative age twist. Traces of all Frobenius powers agree.
Use the characteristic-zero Brauer–Nesbitt recognition on semisimplifications of these virtual classes. No semisimplicity of the original arithmetic action is inferred.
acceptance: I2 and the unipotent Jordan block J2 have identical traces of every power but different fixed-space dimensions; the conclusion must not identify them as actual representations.
An even and an odd copy of the same representation cancel virtually, so virtual equality alone does not separate degrees.

sources.locator: §6.2, Theorem 6.12, p.569; §7.4, proof of Theorem 7.23, p.589, retained with correction E25

Purity of a proper direct-image complex does not automatically make every singular fibre cohomology pure in its ordinary degree, and purity alone does not kill Frobenius Jordan blocks.

Audit any proposed degree separation at the actual singular fibres, rather than infer it from global smoothness of the total space.

Resolving the target must defeat both extension-class ambiguity and alternating-degree cancellation; a semisimple recognition theorem alone defeats neither without its hypotheses.

nodes.title: Determinant variation of inertia-sector traces
nodes.statement: Let ν label the determinant twist of the SL fibration by δ(L Lν⁻¹)∈Γ, so its geometric Frobenius is ν⁻¹Fr. Let Tγ(ν) be the twisted trace of the γ-inertia sector of the corresponding mirror PGL data, including the prescribed degree power of its gerbe and the age twist. With the Weil pairing convention χγ(ν)=(ν,γ), prove Tγ(ν)=(ν,γ)⁻¹Tγ(0).
hypotheses: k contains μ_(n^(2g+1)), Γ is constant and the genus/regular-locus gates of the preceding applications are retained.
The local Tate calculation uses only the ordered mixed block between an unramified ν and the tame sector class. It does not use isotropy of the complementary block at even torsion.
Tγ(ν) includes the transported gerbe and power-of-determinant choices; it is not an unlabelled comparison of fixed loci with unrelated gerbes.
proofSteps: Lift the finite list of determinant line bundles and compare the SL torsor classes by the unramified Γ class ν.
Use the self-dual isogeny exact sequence and its pairing adjunction to identify the ratio of local gerbe characters with the inverse local Tate pairing of ν and the connecting class of a PGL point.

Apply the imported specialization with the inverse tame-character generator convention to identify the ramified coordinate of that connecting class with γ. The mixed evaluation is then the normalized Jacobian Weil pairing (ν,γ).
Integrate on the fixed γ sector and use twisted-integral with its conjugation conventions consistently. This gives the displayed ratio; no vanishing of the ramified/ramified diagonal is needed.
acceptance: For n=3 and (ν,γ)=ζ3, the multiplier is ζ3⁻¹; the direct multiplier fails the fixed ν⁻¹Fr convention.
For F=Q3 and the complementary C2 Kummer class of −3, the diagonal self-pairing can have invariant 1/2. The mixed formula must remain valid without asserting that this diagonal vanishes.

nodes.title: Character-isotypic mirror symmetry
nodes.statement: In the finite-field setting of the main theorem, with Γ constant, choose the primitive nth root and the Jacobian Weil pairing identifying γ∈Γ with χγ(ν)=(ν,γ). Then Tr(Fr,H_c^*(M_SL^L,Qbarℓ)^χγ)=Tr(Fr,H_c^*([(M_SL^L′)^γ/Γ],N_L′⊗Qbarℓ(−Fγ))). Traces are alternating, and the right side is the γ-sector of the PGL inertia with its degree-d powered Hausel–Thaddeus gerbe.
hypotheses: The star denotes the alternating compact-support realization, not a direct sum with forgotten signs.
Use ℓ≠p splitting coefficients, the same faithful μn character and the ν⁻¹Fr convention.
The theorem gives a character trace identity, not the actual-isomorphism claim left in strong-fibre-isomorphism.
proofSteps: Use determinant-twisting to enumerate all Γ twists of the SL space over k. The trace of a twist is Tr(ν⁻¹Fr,H_c^*(M_SL^L)).
Multiply by χγ(ν), sum over ν and divide by |Γ|. The existing pinned character orthogonality isolates the χγ eigenspace; no new generic Fourier theory is needed.
Apply main-mirror to each determinant twist and sector-variation to its mirror trace. The same character orthogonality isolates precisely the γ sector.
Cancel the common factor |Γ|. Keep every age twist, character inverse and stack automorphism weight from the supplying nodes.
acceptance: For Γ=1 recover the ordinary total trace equality.
For C3 the ν⁻¹ action and multiplier χγ(ν), with division by 3, isolate χγ and not its inverse.
For n=2,g=2 the Fourier normalization is 1/16, using all 16 characters.
